Runtime is node:22 with express@5.1.0 and better-sqlite3@12.4.1 preinstalled on NODE_PATH (environment/Dockerfile); /assets/seed_data.json is present in the agent image and instruction.md:15 tells the builder to copy it into /app because /assets is unavailable at runtime; network is public and CDN use is permitted (instruction.md:13, integration.md:12-14). Seed supports every seeded fact a criterion relies on: Lena (USR-CAN3) read_count 2 on APP-301 whose 3rd message is from USR-REC3 -> 1 unread, matching protocol Z; APP-101 has 120 messages, matching app_context.md:30 and hro_thread_latest/earlier; candidate wording and page size 30 are in the seed (hireops_rules.md:207-208). No graded capability is unreachable. Most rules are single-reading and precise (one-stage moves, reject/reopen, bulk board order hireops_rules.md:89-92, undo conflict list :96-100, 401/403/404 :21-23, version-based 409 :77-80, unread/seen definitions :151-166). Checked candidate ambiguities that turned out harmless: (a) whether re-ordering counts as a 'move' for undo-supersession - protocol B(11) is overdetermined because Mei already moved X in B(9), so any reading refuses that undo; (b) whether reopening is an undoable move - settled by ':97 restores a rejection reason that the move removed'; (c) whether hiring managers may add candidates - settled by :31 'A recruiter adds a candidate' and hro_mgr_early_refused; (d) 'get signed out' (instruction.md:7) - explicit sign-out and expiry are both covered by one design and polish hro_pol_session_resume accepts either prompt timing. Ambiguities that change grading: [1, P2] Where per-conversation unread counts appear. Brief: 'Unread counts need to be right for each person' (instruction.md:7); rules: 'Unread counts are shown per conversation and as one total for the person' (hireops_rules.md:154), with Board/Conversations/Activity as separate views (instruction.md:11). The natural reading puts per-conversation counts in the Conversations list and the total in navigation. Functional protocol U (tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:41) says 'Every reading in U is made without reloading, navigating or clicking in Rafael's page ... With Rafael's page on the Board, Tomas sends two messages; read Rafael's count on that conversation and his total', and hro_unread_counts (weight 2 of 58.5) 'Fails if any count is wrong ... or changes only after a reload or navigation'. Only an app that also shows a per-conversation count on the Board can provide that reading. The golden does that (solution/app/public/js/board.js:253, unread badge on each board card), but no public text asks for it. [2, P3] Message arriving while typing at the newest message. instruction.md:7 says 'If a message arrives while I am reading further up or halfway through writing a reply, leave my place, my draft and my cursor alone and just tell me there is something new', which on its face also covers a reader at the bottom who is typing: keep the scroll position and only notify. hireops_rules.md:158 says 'if they are at the newest message, it is shown and counts as read'. Polish hro_pol_live_thread (weight 3) fails if 'the view moves away from the newest message'. An app following instruction.md:7 literally keeps scrollTop fixed, appends the message below the fold and shows a notice. That app can be read as having left the newest message, and it leaves the message unread, which contradicts :158. Most implementers will follow the more specific rule, so the risk is low, but the two public texts read differently. [3, P3] 'keyboard focus stays on that card's controls' (hireops_rules.md:85) versus hro_refused_put_back's '(document.activeElement inside the card)'. If move controls live in an opened card-details panel (allowed: :104 'A card can be opened to show its details'), focus on the panel's move control meets the rule text, but a judge could fail it as not inside the board card element. No configured judge run exists to measure any of these; evidence is source reading plus golden source only.
unresolved.counterexample: A conforming HireOps build: separate Board / Conversations / Activity views (as instruction.md:11 asks), the per-person total unread badge on the Conversations nav item updating live, and per-conversation unread badges in the Conversations list, also live, but no unread badge on board cards. In protocol U the judge holds Rafael's page on the Board and is forbidden to navigate. It sees the total rise by 2 but cannot read 'Rafael's count on that conversation' without navigating to Conversations. Once it navigates, the per-conversation count shows 2 correctly, but the criterion's own text ('changes only after a reload or navigation') invites a 0 on hro_unread_counts (2/58.5 functional weight) for an app that meets every public unread rule. A golden-shaped app passes only because of a board-card badge that no public text requests.
unresolved.suggested_fix: In functional protocol U, either keep Rafael's page on the Conversations list with no conversation open (so both per-conversation and total counts are visible without navigation), or allow the per-conversation reading to be taken by navigating to the conversation list after the 15 s live check on the total. Separately, align instruction.md:7 with hireops_rules.md:156-160 (e.g. 'if I am reading further up, leave my place alone and tell me; if I am at the bottom, show it, but never touch my draft or cursor'), and loosen hro_refused_put_back to 'focus on a control of that card (on the board card or its open details)'.

unresolved.evidence: BRIEF DEMANDS A REAL MULTI-USER PRODUCT. instruction.md:1 asks for a shared recruiting workspace where 'Several of us have it open at once, so the hard part is that nobody's work gets trampled'; :3 one-stage moves with ordinary controls, shared manual ordering, Interview capacity, refusal with put-back and who-changed-it, all-or-none multi-select moves, undo with conflict refusal; :5 live updates within 15 s preserving open card/draft/cursor; :7 paged long conversations with scroll anchoring, per-person unread, seen marks, per-user per-conversation drafts surviving reload and sign-out; :9 candidate portal with data isolation; :13-15 Node/Express/SQLite server, durable DB honouring DB_PATH, seed loaded once, persistence across restart. hireops_rules.md adds roles with 401/403/404 semantics (s1), validation (s2), versioned 409 concurrency (s3 'Two people at once'), bulk/undo rules (s3), immutable activity log (s4), unread/seen arithmetic (s6), candidate-response redaction (s7). The agent image starts empty: environment/Dockerfile:17-23 creates /app holding only .gitkeep; no starter. The frozen golden is ~70 KB of JS (solution/app/src/index.js 26,354 B; public/js/board.js 22,485 B; threads.js 12,283 B; app.js 9,579 B), consistent with substantial build work. SMALLEST SATISFYING SUBMISSION is therefore a full authenticated multi-role server-backed app; no single screen, mock or tweak satisfies the brief. GRADING SEPARATES STUBS: gates/render criterion hro_gate_render requires wrong-password refusal plus real sign-in to a usable workspace ('A static picture or only a health response is insufficient'); gates/constraints hro_gate_shared requires UI-created job + candidate visible to the Observer in an independent browser context ('A static seed response, a no-op success message, a browser-only save or a job-only app does not satisfy the gate'); scoring.toml gates render/constraints = 0.0 and score.py:41-48 zeroes reward unless both gates pass and functional > floor 0.05. Each scored prompt restates the same backend gate (functional prompt.md:11-13, polish prompt.md:11-12, visual prompt.md:11-12 'normalizes to zero'). Functional has 43 binary criteria summing weight 58.5, dominated by rule/concurrency/live/privacy behaviour (e.g. hro_stale_refused 2.5, hro_live_board 2.5, hro_candidate_private 2.5, hro_bulk_all_or_none 2, hro_undo_restores 2, hro_unread_scrolled_up 2, hro_drafts 2), so most mass is unreachable without the hard parts. ADVERSARIAL ATTEMPTS: (1) static mock / seed-copy board -> fails hro_gate_render or hro_gate_shared (no server save visible in independent context) -> reward 0. (2) localStorage-only SPA -> fails hro_gate_shared independent-context readback -> 0. (3) plain single-board CRUD (sign-in, jobs, add candidate, move buttons, no rules/live/conversations) -> passes gates and can exceed the 0.05 floor (2.925 of 58.5 weight) via hro_job_open/add_candidate/arrive_bottom/reorder/restart/anonymous etc.; it earns a bounded partial score (rough source estimate: functional <~0.2 raw -> <~0.12 weighted, polish 0 since all five polish rows need live/conversation behaviour, visual up to 0.2) and cannot approach the golden. That is partial credit for partial real work, not a stub earning the reward; the visual-weight vs. functional-floor balance belongs to rows 39/42/44. CONFORMING ALTERNATIVE: an app using SSE or sockets instead of polling, different routes/labels, hidden rather than disabled controls, or UI-side refusal before sending is explicitly accepted (rules s5 'Polling, server-sent events and sockets are all acceptable'; functional prompt.md:15,23 'Whether a refused action is offered at all is the app's choice', no required routes/selectors), so no row-7 path fails a real build for non-product reasons. RISK=true because the stub-exclusion half ('can't earn the reward') rests on source reasoning only: raw-evidence-index.json scope states 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent'. The scripted golden run (qc/repairs/hireops-2026-10-03-workspace/results/workspace.json, hash verified) is not a judge run and no weak/stub app was graded. This is a measurement gap, not a defect in the ask.

Gates: each 600 < 1500, sum 1200 < 1500 (300 s headroom). Scored: each < 11100, sum 9000+900+900 = 10800 < 11100 (300 s headroom). Budgets: 1500 + 11100 = 12600 < 13200 (600 s headroom for cp of /app, the liveness loop, prompt substitution and two score.py runs). Liveness: test.sh:116-122 120 x 0.25 s sleep with 2 s urlopen timeouts (~30 s for a refused/fast port; worst case on hanging sockets ~510 s, still inside the 600 s verifier headroom, and it runs before the gate budget starts). Restart: generated helper waits 120 x 0.25 s (test.sh:171-182) inside restart_mcp.py HELPER_TIMEOUT_SEC = 55 (tools/restart_mcp.py:11), which sits inside the 9000 s functional judge. tests/test.sh SHA256 bd682592... equals the template test.sh; tests/tools identical to template (diff -r empty); task.toml differs from the template only in [task]/[metadata] identity text, timeouts identical to staged-task-contract.md:54-63,111. Agent image (environment/Dockerfile) is node:22-bookworm-slim + small apt set + npm -g express@5.1.0 better-sqlite3@12.4.1 (prebuilt binary) - a realistic cold build well under 600 s, but not measured here. Agent 7200 s is the canonical value for a hard full-stack build; no agent run measured. 'LONG ENOUGH' HALF (unmeasured). The functional dimension has 43 criteria (grep '[[criterion]]' count) judged in one batched claude-code session driven by a 12.6 KB prompt with 13 multi-context protocols (Z,S,M,L,C,B,N,T,U,V,A,D plus a backend check), many independent browser contexts, several 15-second no-touch waits (U, V) and one restart. Whether GLM-5.3-flashx through claude-code finishes that within 9000 s, and whether the 600 s constraints gate (create job + candidate + independent Observer context) finishes reliably, has not been measured: raw-evidence-index.json scope states 'Full configured grading/workload ... are absent' and every entry is 'Not a configured judge run ... or judge-duration measurement'. The scripted golden (results/workspace.json, 18 groups all passed) is not judge duration (REVIEW_POLICY.md:25). Per SKILL.md 'Never upgrade an unmeasured claim to Pass', the row cannot be Pass. Mitigation present: every prompt instructs NOT EXERCISED - evaluator/tool limitation on exhausted budget (gates/*/prompt.md:11, polish:18, visual:16), but a suite-level `timeout` kill at test.sh:213/224 returns non-zero and exits with the zero reward, so a too-short budget would attribute a harness failure to the submission. Adversarial probes: (a) a broken app cannot exploit the timeouts - a slow/hanging app only consumes judge time and earns NOT EXERCISED zeros, and liveness failure yields zero; (b) a conforming but slow-rendering or many-context-heavy app could push the sequential functional session past 9000 s or the constraints gate past 600 s, collapsing to reward 0 (gate kill) or losing late protocols (A, D restart run last) - plausible, unmeasured. No timeout change is warranted or authorized without a full configured timing measurement (REVIEW_POLICY.md:25; AGENTS.md).

DEFECT (subsumption + contradictory judge instruction): hro_candidate_linked (functional judge.toml:393-399, weight 0.5, 'the card added with Tomas's account email becomes Tomas's application and conversation when he signs in') is strictly subsumed by hro_msg_exchange (judge.toml:294-300, weight 1.5, 'Rafael's message reaches Tomas's independent context'), because protocol T (functional/prompt.md:39) runs the exchange only on 'Tomas's new J2 conversation' created by that linking (fallback J3 is also a linked card). hro_unread_counts (judge.toml:330-336, 2.0: 'On Tomas's new J2 conversation, after Tomas's two messages') and hro_seen (judge.toml:348-354, 1.5: 'after Tomas opens it') and hro_candidate_view's wording-follows-stage leg (judge.toml:375-381, 1.5; protocol K prompt.md:43 moves 'Tomas's J2 card') also require the same linking as setup. Every app that passes hro_msg_exchange passes hro_candidate_linked; a single linking defect is graded in up to five rows (0.5+1.5+2+1.5+1.5 = 7.0 of 58.5 functional weight, ~12% of functional, ~7% of total reward). Meanwhile functional/prompt.md:23 says 'Never deduct one observed defect in more than one row' and prompt.md:13 says re-setup 'on a new job of your own if that is possible without the broken feature', which is impossible here (any Tomas conversation on a new job needs linking) and the seeded Data Analyst conversation is only named as an exclusion (prompt.md:39 'not his Data Analyst one'), so the judge has two incompatible instructions: fail the dependent rows on the observed linking defect, or refrain from double deduction and leave them unobserved/passed. Scoring of the same app can therefore differ by up to 7 weight points depending on which instruction the judge follows. This is the 'subsume each other' case in the workbook wording, not the permitted 'one criterion covering a whole flow' bundle (SKILL.md known false positives), and REVIEW_POLICY.md 'Independent credit takes precedence over flow grouping ...
